transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2028-04-11 14:30 PT
Duration: ~57 minutes
Recording: Zoom
Attendees: Morgan Hayes (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Tess Rowland (Redwood SE), Jules Park (Sentinel CTO), Ruth Chang (Sentinel Head of Infra), Eli Novak (Security), Marco Diaz (ML Lead)

Summary (auto):
Quick POC scoping focused on private connectivity options (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), residency/region constraints, workload sizing for a mid-size production traffic pattern, and an agreed benchmark plan and 4-week timeline. Action items captured.

00:00 Morgan: Okay hi everybody good afternoon, thanks for joining. we have about an hour. real quick intros?
00:12 Jules: Jules Park here, CTO at Sentinel. we're trying to validate a private deployment for inference - main ask is data never leaves region and egress is tightly restricted.
00:20 Ruth: Ruth - infra. We'll own peering / network side and need to understand peering vs privatelink operational tradeoffs.
:29 Eli: Eli from security - SOC2 + KMS + audit logs are the big ones for us.
00:36 Morgan: Great thanks. Samir and Tess from our side will walk through sizing and benchmark approach. high level goal: a 4-week pilot to validate perf and networking isolation, and run a small sample of production traffic.
01:05 Samir: Quick clarifying question - Marco you mentioned a mid-size latency sensitive workload in the note. what's your p95 latency target and qps?
01:12 Marco: We're aiming for p95 <250ms on generation responses for the chat endpoint with typical seq lengths ~1k tokens, bursts up to 40 qps sustained for 10 minutes.
01:25 Samir: okay that's helpful. are you streaming tokens to the client?
01:29 Marco: yes streaming. client expects chunked responses so we need to validate streaming latency and ordering.
02:10 Tess: for the POC we'll test two model variants: a 7B quantized variant and a 13B float16. plan is to compare latency/cost and regression on a holdout eval set.
02:33 Jules: for residency, main constraint: model weights can be outside region but inference MUST occur in eu-west-1. we also want all telemetry and logs to be retained for 90 days within our account.
02:50 Ruth: also egress control: we can only allow egress to specific partner endpoints, everything else blocked.
03:08 Morgan: ok noted. on network patterns - we typically offer two private connectivity patterns: VPC peering (direct) and PrivateLink (endpoint) for AWS. pros/cons: peering has simpler routing and lower egress hops but needs cross-account route management; PrivateLink isolates at NLB level and gives tighter control but can add an extra hop and NAT in some topologies.
03:42 Ruth: what's the typical latency delta you see between peering and privatelink?
03:48 Samir: in our measurements it's often 5-25ms depending on region and topology; less predictable if transit through NAT or if IP translations happen — sometimes the transcript system picks that up as "pairing" but i mean peering, sorry.
04:15 Eli: about encryption - we need customer-managed KMS for any at-rest model artifacts and envelope encryption for logs. can Redwood support CMK?
04:26 Morgan: yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations. we'll include the integration checklist in the security packet.
04:40 Marco: for bench metrics we want tokens-per-second, p50/p95 latency, cold-starts, and GPU util during sustained bursts. also need to track cost per 1M tokens as a baseline.
05:02 Samir: agreed. our suggested matrix: run each model variant on two instance types (A40-class and H100-class equivalence), sequence lengths of 256/512/1024, sustained qps at 5/20/40, each run 10 minutes with 2-minute warmup. capture KV cache hit behavior as well.
05:25 Jules: can you run with prefix caching on vs off? our traffic has long repeated prefixes in the prompt templates.
05:30 Tess: yes we'll include prefix/KV cache on/off as a factor. that usually shows big gains for repeated context.
06:01 Ruth: on networking - we prefer privatelink because it aligns with our least-privilege posture, but we worry about additional network egress charges and complexity. does Redwood have a recommended landing zone template?
06:18 Morgan: we do - landing zone + CF/Terraform modules for privatelink endpoints, route tables, security groups and flow logs. we'll push the repo link.
06:27 Ruth: great, send that.
06:35 Marco: timeline question - how long to stand up a private deployment for a pilot?
06:39 Morgan: typical is 2 weeks to provision infra and landing zone (accounts, peering/privatelink, KMS bindings), then 1 week for model onboarding and basic smoke tests, then 1 week of benchmark runs and tuning = 4 weeks end-to-end. if you have infra folks ready it can be compressed.
07:05 Samir: one callout - if you want to test on H100-class we'd prefer scheduled window due to capacity; otherwise A40-class equiv is more readily available.
07:20 Jules: cost sensitivity - if H100 is required to meet p95 we'd like to see cost trade-offs. include cost-per-hour and cost-per-1M tokens in the report.
07:31 Tess: will do.
07:40 Eli: audit logging - do you provide tenant-level audit logs shipped to our S3 bucket? we need immutable logs for 90 days plus retention policy controls.
07:53 Morgan: yes, Redwood Private can forward audit logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies. we'll document retention and immutability options.
08:10 Marco: edge case - if peering is used and we need region-failsafe, can we do cross-region fallback? we want to lock to eu-west-1 but have a DR plan that maybe fails to eu-central-1 in emergencies.
08:28 Samir: we can route by policy and have fallback model variants pinned in other regions, but that changes residency guarantees. you would need an exception for DR and explicit approvals.
08:40 Ruth: that's fine as long as fallback is auditable and we can toggle it.
09:02 Morgan: let's outline the benchmark acceptance criteria — what would count as success for the POC?
09:10 Jules: acceptance: p95 <250ms streaming end-to-end for the 7B quantized with cache enabled at 40 qps bursts; functional parity on the holdout eval (no >2% regression on quality metrics); network isolation validated with privatelink; audit logs ingested and KMS validated.
09:30 Samir: ok noted. also add operational: stable CPU/GPU utilization under burst with no worker OOMs and <1% error rate for request failures in test windows.
09:46 Marco: also include tokenization/throughput metrics and cold-start <3s target for scale-up from 0.
10:05 Morgan: sounds good. we'll codify that in the SOW.
10:20 Tess: on benchmarking mechanics - we prefer coordinating a 2-hour window where Sentinel exposes a test harness in a private subnet and we run generator clients from Redwood's test bastion via the privatelink endpoint. that minimizes external egress.
10:43 Ruth: that works. security will want to watch the tests. Eli - you'll be available right?
10:50 Eli: yes i'll join the run window and will tail logs for any unexpected outbound connections.
11:02 Marco: can we also run a simulated spike at 120 qps for 60s to see graceful degradation behavior?
11:10 Samir: yes we'll include a soak and a spike test. we'll capture metrics and a failure-mode analysis.
11:24 Morgan: on data residency - you said model weights can be outside region but you want inference inside. confirm: are we allowed to pull model shards from S3 in another region during load?
11:33 Jules: no, we'd prefer model weights cached in eu-west-1 or pulled in a pre-warm step; net egress for shards from other regions is not allowed.
11:45 Samir: ok we'll onboard model artifact into a region-local bucket or use a customer-provided ECR/S3 in eu-west-1. we'll note that in onboarding runbook.
12:00 Tess: small note: quantized variants may be slightly lower quality on some edge prompts; we'll include an eval rubric and sample failures.
12:14 Marco: good to have that ahead of time.
12:22 Morgan: any concerns about compliance?
12:25 Eli: SOC2 is baseline; we also need details on key rotation cadence, HSM provider, and whether logs can be forwarded to Splunk in addition to S3.
12:36 Morgan: yes we support Splunk/syslog forwarding and will include key rotation details in the packet.
12:50 Ruth: on privatelink charges, any ballpark? we need to include network cost in POC budget.
12:58 Samir: depends on bandwidth. for planning assume X cents per GB plus endpoint-hour cost; we'll provide a rough estimator in the SOW.
13:12 Jules: ok. one more thing - does Redwood provide any tooling to replay production traces for bench?
13:18 Tess: we have a lightweight replay harness and will adapt it for your payload format. Marco, we'll need the sample traces.
13:27 Marco: will share 48 hours.
13:35 Morgan: great. recap quick: POC acceptance criteria captured, benchmark matrix agreed, landing zone + privatelink template to be delivered, security packet and SOW by Friday, run window week of April 23. anyone disagree?
13:54 Jules: sounds good.
14:00 Eli: good.
14:05 Ruth: yep.
14:10 Morgan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with calendar invites and the SOW.
